---
title: "*Data Feminism* & Design Justice"
subtitle: "How do our choices shape whose culture becomes data?"

## In-Class Agenda

- How do our choices shape what culture becomes data? What are some of the tradeoffs?
- Binaries and complex phenomena
- Histories of Power and Missingness
- Debate: when should we use categories versus capture data fully

## Assigned Materials

- D’Ignazio, Catherine, and Lauren F. Klein. “‘What Gets Counted Counts.’” In *Data Feminism*, by Catherine D’Ignazio and Lauren F. Klein. The MIT Press, 2020. [https://doi.org/10.7551/mitpress/11805.001.0001](https://doi.org/10.7551/mitpress/11805.001.0001).
- D’Ignazio, Catherine, and Lauren F. Klein. “The Power Chapter.” In *Data Feminism*. The MIT Press, 2020. [https://direct.mit.edu/books/oa-monograph/4660/chapter/213285/The-Power-Chapter](https://direct.mit.edu/books/oa-monograph/4660/chapter/213285/The-Power-Chapter).
- Trejo, Sylvia Fernández and Paulina Hernandez. “Gender Violence at the Border (1993-1998) – *Responsible Datasets in Context*.” *Responsible Datasets in Context*, August 1, 2024. [https://www.responsible-datasets-in-context.com/posts/gender-violence/](https://www.responsible-datasets-in-context.com/posts/gender-violence/).
